# Normal semisimple subgroups generated by commuting root partitions

Over an algebraically closed field, let `G` be semisimple with a supplied split
maximal torus. Every subset of its actual roots commuting with the complement
on all scheme tests generates an actual closed normal semisimple subgroup.
`RootPartitionNormalModel` retains this subgroup, its inclusion, containment
of the selected root groups, minimality in arbitrary closed competitors, and
centrality of every complementary root group. Models for disjoint root parts
centralize each other as full subgroup functors.

The construction uses the published smooth connected generated-family
construction applied to the actual smooth connected root-group
representatives. Complementary root groups centralize each generator, hence
the generated group. Selected root groups lie in the group and normalize it.
Consequently every actual root group lies in its normalizer. The normalizer
is closed, and semisimple root generation makes it the entire ambient group.
The published normal-subgroup semisimplicity theorem then gives semisimplicity
of the generated group. Minimality and closed representability of centralizers
give the final comparison for disjoint parts.

This is an internally derived construction from published generated-family,
root-generation, normal-subgroup and centralizer theorems. It prepares the
field component-factor comparison in the route motivated by Conrad,
*Reductive group schemes* (2014), Proposition 6.4.4, pp.232–233. No almost
simplicity, arbitrary-base construction or product isomorphism is asserted.
